newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-THREE K'S SET SEASON'S BESTS IN ROME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-THREE K'S SET SEASON'S BESTS IN ROME.

text.p: Kenyan Daniel Komen, racing on a rainy night in Rome, on Thursday became the first man this year to run the 5,000 metres in under 13 minutes.

He was joined in setting season's best times at the Golden Gala athletics Grand Prix by compatriot Moses Kiptanui in the 3,000 metres steeplechase and Kenyan-born Dane Wilson Kipketer in the 800 metres.
Cuban Ivan Pedroso and Jamaican James Beckford also leaped 8.48 metres to set season's bests in the long jump.

Kenya's Lidia Cheromei set a season's best in the women's 5,000 with a time of 14:49.37 for the first sub-15 minute time of the year, finishing ahead of Portuguese world record holder Fernanda Ribeiro who had a time of 14:55.78.
The three K's provided the highlights at a mostly empty Olympic stadium with the big-name Americans absent due to the coming U.S trials for the world championships in Athens in August.
Running as occasional flashes of lightning lit the sky, Komen clocked 12 minutes 48.98 seconds.
That marked a huge improvement on his previous season's best time of 13:03.51 set in Osaka on May 10.
"I think I can go even faster," he said.
The race also brought the 21-year-old victory in what was billed as a battle with Morocco's Salah Hissou.
Hissou also ran a sub-13 minute race, clocking 12:52.39 after jostling for the lead with Komen on the last lap.
Komen led Hissou at the bell but the Moroccan took the lead coming out of the curve. Komen then forged ahead again on the straight and accelerated away to the line.
Kipketer, in his first real 800 metres test since he shattered the indoor record at the world championships in Paris in March, clocked one minute 43.54 seconds.
The year's previous best outdoor time of 1:44.4 was set by Kenya's Vincent Malakwen in Nairobi last month.
Kipketer, the world champion who was not allowed to run for his adopted country Denmark at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, has an indoor record of 1:42.67.
The heavy rain made any attempt on Briton Sebastian Coe's 16-year-old world record of 1:41.73 out of the question but Kipketer's time gave the crowd something to cheer about.
Kiptanui, who holds the steeplechase world record of 7:59.18 and had declared before the race that he hoped to run another sub-eight minute time, was optimistic given the weather.

"The conditions weren't good for steeplechase...I could have gone under eight minutes if it hadn't been raining," said Kiptanui, whose time of 8:07.50 leapfrogged him ahead of Kipketer's previous season's mark of 8:08.36.

Russian double Olympic champion Svetlana Masterkova, also racing her first real 800 metres test of the season, could manage no better than third place after being overtaken in the final metres in a race won by Olympic rival Ana Quirot of Cuba.
Masterkova led off the final bend but then faded. Quirot's time of 1:58.70 was the fifth fastest of the year, although the season is yet in its infancy.

Briton Linford Christie won his 100 metres sprint heat on a photofinish but otherwise slow 10.20 seconds. The former Olympic champion was slower than the winner of the B group, Nigerian Francis Obikwelu in 10.15.

Namibian Frankie Fredericks won the 200 metres in a respectable 20.24 seconds, an expected result after main rival Ato Boldon of Trinidad pulled out of the Grand Prix earlier in the week due to a muscle twinge in his left leg.
Britain's former Olympic champion Sally Gunnell returned to serious action after injury at the Atlanta Olympics and finished fifth fastest in 55.59 seconds in the 400 metres hurdles.
"Its good to be back," she said, adding that she had no problems with the injury.
"But I'm not sure about the future. I'll only be going (to Athens) if I can win a medal."
